SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - NOT LAW. Written for the evalgate test suite only.

Fixture guidance for importers

1 Purpose
This guidance explains, in plain language, what an importer has to do under
Fixture Regulation A. It has no legal force and is written only so that the
test suite has a document whose register differs from the instruments.

2 Who has to report
If you import cement, electricity, fertilisers, iron and steel, aluminium or
hydrogen, you are a reporting declarant. If you only import consignments worth
less than EUR 150 in total, you do not have to report.

3 When to report
Reports are quarterly. You have one month after each quarter ends. If you miss
something, you can still correct a report for two months after the deadline,
and the first two quarters have a longer correction window.

4 What to report
Report how much of each good you imported and the emissions embedded in it. If
you cannot get real emissions figures from your supplier, you may use the
default values, but only for imports up to 31 July 2024.

5 Getting authorised
Authorisation is separate from reporting. Apply through the registry with your
registration number. The authority has 120 days to decide, and that clock stops
while it waits for information from you. Authorisation is free.

6 Common mistakes
The most common error is reporting electricity in tonnes. Electricity is
reported in megawatt hours. The second most common error is assuming that
default values remain available after the transitional period.
